## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

# Epic: Completed/audited work items resurface as open (re-sort timestamp churn + parent demotion)

## Problem statement

Multiple work items that were audited and completed (e.g. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V with "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03, WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2, WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC) reappear in the open/planning queues, looking like duplicates or revivals of finished work. Investigation (2026-09-11) found two independent by-design mechanisms stacking:

1. **Re-sort bulk-touches `updatedAt`.** `batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) stamps one shared `now` onto every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` unless `--no-re-sort`. Evidence: 13 items sharing identical `updatedAt=2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z` with consecutive sortIndex 300-1500; another 88-item cluster at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`. The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) means a re-sort after an audit silently invalidates it — WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's passing audit is now stale, and WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC merely *looks* freshly revived via rewritten `updatedAt`/recency.
2. **Parent demotion on late child attach.** `demoteParentOnChildAdded` (`database.ts:1566-1585`, via `create.ts:252-286`, `update.ts:489`) rewinds any `completed`/`in_review` parent to `open`/`plan_complete` when a child is added — with no comment recording why. Evidence: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V demoted when WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK attached 2026-09-06 (after passing audit); WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 kept non-terminal when the triage bot auto-attached WL-0MTUOJLA9008JSTZ (`[test-failure]`) 2026-09-09.

## Users

- **Producer/operator triaging the queue:** wants `wl next` / `wl recent` to show genuinely actionable work, not zombie revivals of audited items.
- **Agents/dispatchers:** should not re-dispatch or re-audit items whose only "change" is a sortIndex rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits: an item audited "Ready to close: Yes" stays audit-fresh across subsequent auto re-sorts that make no semantic change.
- [ ] Attaching a bot-created child (test-failure, triage) to a completed/in_review parent does not silently rewind the parent; any demotion that does fire leaves a comment on the parent recording cause.
- [ ] Queue surfaces (`wl next`, `wl recent`, heartbeat selection) distinguish semantic edits from mechanical timestamp churn.
- [ ] Existing re-sort, demotion, audit-freshness, and sync tests still pass; new regression tests cover: re-sort preserves audit freshness, bot-child attach behavior, demotion audit-trail comment.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Do not break the `auditedAt >= updatedAt` freshness invariant for genuine semantic edits — only mechanical churn (sortIndex-only) must be excluded.
- Demotion behavior for human-added missed subtasks (the original WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 intent) must be preserved.
- Keep changes surgical in `packages/shared/src/` + `src/commands/`; no schema migration unless unavoidable.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (timestamp stamping)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort`, `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, `assignSortIndexValuesForItems`
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`, `src/commands/create.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — heartbeat selection on `updatedAt`-adjacent ordering

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (audit freshness rule)
- WL-0MSN7ORM6005IOW5 (stuck stage/status on audit-completed items — possibly same root cause)

# Child 1: Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits via `updatedAt` churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` stamps `updatedAt = now` alongside `sortIndex` in a single SQL UPDATE:

```sql
UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ? WHERE id = ?
```

This means any re-sort operation (triggered automatically on `wl next` unless `--no-re-sort`) bumps the `updatedAt` of every item whose sortIndex changed. The audit-freshness rule (`isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `database.ts:644`) checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt` — so a re-sort after an audit silently invalidates a previously passing audit.

**Evidence:** 13 items share identical `updatedAt=2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z` with consecutive sortIndex 300-1500; another 88-item cluster at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's passing audit is stale after re-sort.

## Root cause

Sort index is an organizational/concern, not a semantic change. The `updatedAt` field is used by the audit freshness invariant as a proxy for "when did this item last change semantically". Stamping `updatedAt` during sortIndex-only updates conflates mechanical churn with semantic edits.

## Solution

Remove `updatedAt = ?` from the sortIndex-only UPDATE in `batchUpdateSortIndices`. This is a surgical change to a single SQL statement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` does NOT update `updatedAt` — sortIndex changes are transparent to audit freshness
- [ ] An item with a passing audit (`readyToClose: true`) retains audit freshness across re-sort operations (auditedAt >= updatedAt still holds)
- [ ] Genuine semantic edits (description, title, status, etc.) still bump `updatedAt` — the freshness invariant works correctly for real changes
- [ ] Existing tests for updatedAt preservation (whitespace-only diffs, CAS claims, etc.) still pass
- [ ] New regression test: audit item → re-sort → verify audit still fresh
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Constraints

- Minimal change: only modify the SQL in `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- Do not break the existing updatedAt preservation behavior for genuine edits (the update/import/upsert no-op guards already handle this)
- No schema migration needed
- The `reSort` function in database.ts calls `assignSortIndexValuesForItems` → `batchUpdateSortIndices`; only the SQL statement changes

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line ~747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort`, `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `assignSortIndexValuesForItems`
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` — existing updatedAt tests

## Parent AC coverage

- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC1:** Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits — this is the primary fix.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC3:** Queue surfaces distinguish semantic edits from mechanical timestamp churn — fixing updatedAt churn at the source enables this.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC4:** New regression test: audit → re-sort → verify freshness.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC5:** Full suite passes (all children contribute).

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9

- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt — sibling symptom)
- WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 (demotion feature — intent to preserve)

# Intake Brief: Client retry does not honor Retry-After (503 startup_ramp)

## Problem statement

The llm-proxy's **post-restart startup ramp** gate returns HTTP `503` with a
randomized `Retry-After` header (5-18 s) and a machine-readable body
(`{"error":{"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."},"status":503,"retry_after":N}`)
specifically so that clients spread their reconnects across the ramp window
(`startup_ramp.max_seconds: 180` in `proxy/config.yaml`; proxy side tracked as
LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX).

The Pi client does **not** honor that hint. Its *agent-level* auto-retry
(`getRetrySettings()` -> `retryDelayMs() = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`,
`baseDelayMs` default 2000 ms, cap 60 000 ms, **no jitter**) ignores both the
`Retry-After` header and the `retry_after` body field.

### Evidence (2026-09-20)

Proxy restarted at 16:11:28 local; the 180 s startup ramp was active until
~16:14:28. Session `herdr-1789917126-2590234-11663` (model `plan`, provider
`Local Proxy`), every turn failing with
`503: {"type":"startup_ramp",...}`:

| attempt | time (local) | gap vs prev |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| 1       | 16:12:10.5   | -           |
| 2       | 16:12:12.6   | +2.0 s      |
| 3       | 16:12:16.6   | +4.0 s      |
| 4       | 16:12:24.6   | +8.0 s      |
| 5       | 16:12:40.7   | +16.0 s     |
| 6       | 16:13:12.8   | +32.1 s     |
| 7       | 16:14:13.1   | +60.3 s     |

This is exactly `2000 * 2^(attempt-1)` capped at 60 000 ms - the client's own
deterministic backoff, independent of the `Retry-After` values the proxy
returned (random randint in [5,15] + 3 s margin per request, logged by the
proxy as `Startup ramp: deferring chat request (... retry_after=Ns)`).

A second session (`herdr-1789917234-2590706-9592`, this very analysis session)
shows the same `+2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0` pattern.

## Impact

1. Clients retry **sooner than instructed** (e.g. `Retry-After: 7` -> retry at
   2 s), hammering the freshly restarted proxy - the opposite of the ramp's
   intent.
2. Backoff has **no jitter**, so clients that started together retry in
   lockstep, defeating the ramp's desynchronisation goal.
3. The retry cap (`maxAgentDelayMs` 60 s) is shorter than the ramp window (up
   to 180 s), so a client can exhaust its retry budget mid-ramp and surface a
   hard failure to the user even though the server said "retry shortly".

## Users

- Operators/developers running herdr workers (Pi agents) against the local
  llm-proxy.
- Anyone whose first provider request after a mode switch / proxy restart lands
  inside the ramp window.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: When an OpenAI-compatible provider response carries `Retry-After`
  (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) and the request is retried, the client's delay is
  at least the server-requested delay (bounded by a configurable maximum,
  default 60 s).
- **AC2**: The `503 startup_ramp` body's `retry_after` field is honored as a
  fallback when the header is absent or unparseable.
- **AC3**: Missing/malformed hints fall back to the existing exponential
  backoff, unchanged.
- **AC4**: A client can survive a full startup ramp (up to
  `startup_ramp.max_seconds`, default 180 s) without exhausting its retry budget,
  or the ramp window is otherwise communicated so a long ramp does not surface
  as a final user-visible failure solely because the retry budget ran out first.
- **AC5**: Jitter is applied to (or combined with) any delay derived from the
  server hint so concurrent clients do not retry in lockstep.
- **AC6**: Tests cover header/body parsing, the cap, malformed values, and the
  long-ramp case; full suite green.
- **AC7**: No double-retry amplification between the provider-level and
  agent-level retry layers.

## Constraints

- Tracked in ContextHub; the change belongs in the **Pi coding agent codebase**
  (same arrangement as WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO).
- Pi already exposes a provider-level helper that *does* honor
  `retry-after`/`retry-after-ms` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` -> `retryProviderRequest`),
  but it is effectively disabled: `openai-completions` calls it with
  `maxRetries` from `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, which is unset
  (-> 0). The active layer is the agent-level retry in `settings-manager` /
  `agent-session` / `retry.ts`, which ignores the hint. Reuse/extend the
  existing helper rather than adding a third retry path.
- Keep the change minimal; do not regress the completed
  WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO tuning. Note: the installed build observed here still
  shows `baseDelayMs = 2000` (not 7000), so verify version drift before
